Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others
on 27 November, 2024 
Author: Sujit Narayan Prasad
Bench: Sujit Narayan Prasad, Navneet Kumar
 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
 W.P.(Cr.) (Db) (Hb) No.460 of 2024
 -----
Dhananjay Kumar Pandey ... ... Petitioner Versus The State of Jharkhand & Others ... ...
Respondents 
-------
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sujit Narayan Prasad Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Navneet
Kumar 
-------
For the Petitioner : Mr. Nawal Kishor Pandey, Advocate For the State : Mr. Deepankar Roy, Ac to
G.A.-Iii For the Resp. No.6 : Mr. Anand Kumar Sinha, Advocate
------
th Order No. 06/Dated 27 November, 2024
1.  The writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed seeking following directions :-
a. Issuance of appropriate writ(s) order(s) / direction(s) in nature of Habeas Corpus for direction upon the respondents to immediately produce "X", wife of Dhananjay Kumar Pandey (petitioner) aged about 24 years (now in custody of Ayodhya Singh Chouhan) against her will, before this Hon'ble Court. b. Issuance of appropriate writ(s)/order(s)/ direction(s) upon respondents to allow the petitioner to have the custody of his wife above named. c. Issuance of appropriate writ(s)/order(s)/
direction(s) upon respondents for providing protection to the petitioner and his family members who are under threat of unpleasant consequences. 
2. The brief facts of the case as per the pleadings made in the writ petition which are required to be enumerated, read as under :-

1 It is the case of the petitioner that the girl, aged about 24 years, is the legally wedded wife of the petitioner. Their marriage has been performed in pursuance of their sweet will on 30.04.2024 in Aarya Samaj Mandir, Gaziyabad (Uttar Pradesh). They have also registered their marriage on 30.04.2024 before the Marriage Registration Officer, District Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh. 
After solemnization of their marriage on 30.04.2024, the petitioner and his wife have telephonically contacted to their family on 01.05.2024 for giving information of marriage then the petitioner got information that the father and the family members of the girl are giving threatening to the father and other family members of the petitioner.
It is the further case of the petitioner that the family of the petitioner was under heavy pressure and threat by the illegal activities of the father of the girl and the local police have also indulged with them and pressurized the family of the petitioner to bring back both the petitioner and the girl. 
Under such circumstances, the petitioner and his wife returned to Dhanbad on 03.05.2024 and appeared in the Kenduadih Police Station, District Dhanbad. 
On their return, the concerned police had called the family members of his wife and forcefully handed over her custody against the wish of his wife and the petitioner. 
It is the case of the petitioner that the father and his family members are torturing to the wife of the petitioner and putting pressure upon her to deny the marriage. They are threatening to kill her. On 05.05.2024 at about 7.40 A.M. the petitioner lastly called her then she stated that they will kill her and she requested for protection. She also told that her family is making a conspiracy to kill the petitioner and his family members. She also stated to the petitioner that they are not giving her sufficient food and are putting pressure on her to obtain divorce from the petitioner. They have also snatched the mobile phone of the girl and now she has been deprived from all means of communications. 
The petitioner has got information that the family members of the girl are searching a boy within their community for solemnization of her marriage against her wishes.
It is the further case of the petitioner that the father of the girl has kept her in illegal detention and forceful custody and the petitioner has reasonable apprehension that the father and family members of his wife may kill her. 
The petitioner, with his apprehension, the petitioner approached to Kenduadih Police Station Dhanbad and requested to protect the life of his wife and to ensure the release of his wife from illegal custody of her father and family members. The petitioner also requested for protection of his life and family members' life. The petitioner also Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105646308/
2 approached to the Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad and the Senior Superintendent of Police Dhanbad and made representation but no action has been taken till date. 
In the above backdrop, the instant writ petition has been filed. 
3. The matter was heard by this Court on 21.11.2024 and after hearing the parties, following order was passed :- 
"Reference has been made of the order dated 01.08.2024, whereby and whereunder the co-ordinate Bench has passed the following order:- 
'IN CHAMBER' "The corpus 'Mst. P' has been produced before us by the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad, in pursuance of the order dated 30.07.2024. The corpus/girl is admittedly 24 years of age. 
2. We have heard the corpus, father and mother of the corpus and the petitioner, who are present in person. No one has disputed the marriage certificate. The father of the girl submits that he is a supplier of the petty contract and use to supply building material and he is also attached with BMS which is a registered Trade Union. 
3. We are not commenting much on what has been stated by the corpus/girl. So far as the parents are concerned, they stated that it is the question of their honor as they belong from a different caste than that of the boy. 
4. The petitioner/boy stated that he is in love with the corpus and the marriage has been solemnized. 
He states that there is continuous threat upon him, on his family members including his sister and brother in law from the father and other family members of the family of the corpus. 
5. We have confronted with the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad. 
6. We direct the Senior Superintendent of Police Dhanbad to initiate an enquiry and submit a report to this Court in a sealed cover about the allegation of torture, threat and threat perception upon the petitioner and his parents or other family members from the side of family members of the corpus. 
7. It is made clear that the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad, will make the parents of the girl understand that if any untowards incident happens to the girl or any of the family members of the petitioner, they will be primarily held responsible. The Senior Superintendent of Police,
Dhanbad, will ensure safety of the corpus/girl and the petitioner/boy and will take appropriate measures as per the situation. 
8. The father and the mother of the girl who are present today, submitted that since they have received a notice, they will engage a Lawyer. 
Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105646308/
3 9. Personal appearance is dispensed with. 
10. Awaiting report, list this case after two months."
2. It is evident from paragraph-6 of the said order that the Senior Superintendent of Police,
Dhanbad is directed to initiate an enquiry and submit a report to this Court in a sealed cover about the allegation of torture, threat and threat perception upon the petitioner and his parents or other family members from the side of family members of the corpus. 
3. In paragraph 7, an observation has been made by the co-ordinate Bench holding the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad responsible for any untowards incident happens to the girl or any of the family members of the petitioner. 
4. Further in paragraph 8, father and mother of the girl have undertaken that since they have received a notice, they will engage a lawyer. 
5. None is appearing for the respondent No.6 either personally or through counsel in pursuance to the undertaking given by the father of the girl as per the order dated 01.08.2024. 
6. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has submitted at BAR that the matter was heard on 01.08.2024 by this Court and submitted that the statements of the corpus/girl, petitioner/boy,
father and mother have been recorded, but we have found nothing on record. 
7. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has further submitted that the marriage has been solemnized with the corpus/girl by the petitioner/boy and to that effect, the marriage certificate has been issued and so long as the marriage certificate is there, the marriage of the corpus/girl and the petitioner is legal one. The petitioner and the corpus/girl are major but the respondent no.6 confined the corpus/girl in his house, has even not been allowed to come out from the house, so that she could meet the petitioner/husband. 
8. It appears from the order dated 01.08.2024, particularly paragraph 3, while considering the statements of the parents of the corpus/girl, it has been recorded therein, that the question of their honor is there, since she belong to a different caste to that of the petitioner/husband. 
9. The writ petition since has been filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for restoration of Habeas Corpus and as such considering the statements so recorded in order dated 01.08.2024 of the parents, as taken note by the co-ordinate Bench in paragraph No.3, wherein the parents have stated that it is the question of their honor as they belong to a different caste than that of the boy. 
10. As such, we are of the view that the respondent No.6, the father is admitting the allegation of the confinement of the corpus/girl in his house, otherwise such statements could not be made before the co- ordinate Bench of this Court in order dated 01.08.2024. 
Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105646308/
4 11. Since the power conferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is invoked and we are dealing with the issue of liberty of the corpus/girl, which is the fundamental right as provided under Article 21 of the Constitution of India and as such, merely because the question of honor of the family is there, the liberty of a citizen cannot be infringed.
12. The Senior Superintendent of Police is directed to again produce the corpus/girl along with mother and father on 27th November 2024 along with the report as directed by this Court as taken note in paragraph -6 of the order dated 01.08.2024 thereof and on that date, the petitioner will also remain present.
13. Since there is specific direction passed by the co- ordinate Bench in paragraph 6 as referred in order dated 01.08.2024 and thereafter the petitioner has brought to the notice of the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad that she was again threatened on 30.08.2024, but it is very unfortunate on the part of the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad even though there is specific direction on, has been passed in his presence, has submitted no report in that respect. 
14. This Court has considered the said conduct of the SSP, Dhanbad very unfortunate, but before passing further necessary order, we are granting one indulgence to the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad, as to why, the order dated 01.08.2024 passed by this Court to submit report regarding the threat perception upon the petitioner and family members, has not been complied with. 
15. Let affidavit be filed along with an explanation on or before the next date of hearing.
16. Let this matter be listed on 27th November 2024 'IN CHAMBER' at 10.30 AM." 
4. Mr. Deepankar Roy, learned A.C. to G.A.-III, has sought leave of this court to allow him to file affidavit in pursuance to the order dated 21.11.2024. 
5. Such leave is granted. 
6. The said affidavit is taken on record. 
7. Considering the averments made in the affidavit, the same is not being accepted. 
8. Mr. Anand Kumar Sinha, learned counsel has put his appearance on behalf of Respondent No.6. 
9. Mr. Anand Kumar Sinha, learned counsel appearing for the Respondent No.6, has submitted that the petitioner has set out false and fabricated story regarding the marriage of the daughter of the Respondent No.6 being solemnized with the petitioner and in fact the girl has been enticed away by the petitioner for ulterior motive and the story of marriage is thoroughly false and fabricated. 
10. He has further submitted that the daughter of the Respondent No.6, as per her own free will and accord, has filed original suit being O.S. No.972 of 2024 in the court of Principal Judge, Family Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105646308/
5 Court, Dhanbad under Section 12(2)(b) of the Hindu Marriage Act for annulment of so called marriage declaring the same to be null and void.
11. It has further been submitted that it is incorrect to say that the Respondent no.6 has confined the girl in his house and not allowing her to come out from the house but the fact of the matter is that the girl is staying with her family as per her own free will.
12. However, he is fair enough to submit that if the girl wants to go with the petitioner, with whom she has solemnized marriage, he will be the last person to make any objection taking into consideration the fact that both the petitioner and the girl/wife are major. 
13. He has further submitted that let an interaction be made with the girl and her family members. 
14. Prior to calling the father and mother of the girl, the petitioner and the girl to whom the marriage has been solemnized as per the pleading made in the petition, we have interacted at length with the girl. 
15. Initially this Court has interacted with the girl alone. She has confessed that she has emotionally been blackmailed by her father and mother by saying so many things like - if she will go along with the petitioner then they will commit suicide and the relationship of the married sister will also break and so many other things including negative things would happen in the family to terrorize the girl. 
16. She has also stated that due to the said conduct, even she was once beaten. She has further stated that she is having feeling/emotion for the petitioner and she wants to live in order to lead the happy married life with the petitioner. But, due to fear of the father and other family members, who are also threatening the family members of the petitioner, she has even been forced to file application under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act before the Family Court, Dhanbad which has been registered as O.S. No.972 of 2024. 
17. The girl has also stated that she is a Graduate and she will manage her life but the thing is that since she is being compelled not to lead the married life with the petitioner and, as such, she has decided under duress, mental agony and fear not to solemnize marriage and in case of any depression, said to be acute in nature, she even can commit suicide. 
18. This Court, thereafter, has called upon the father and the mother of the girl and the learned counsel representing the parties. 
19. The moment the father of the girl has entered, the Court asked him to take seat. The mother of the girl has also been asked to take her seat. But as per the arrangement one chair was vacant in between the petitioner and the girl. The girl has tried to accommodate the mother by vacating the seat upon which she was sitting in order to shift in the chair adjacent to petitioner so that the mother may sit just adjacent to the father. But upon this, the father has behaved rudely by asking the girl not to change her seat otherwise she would have nearer to the petitioner. The voice was loud full of anguish and arrogance and commanding also. 
Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105646308/
6 20. This Court, after having heard the same from the mouth of the father of the girl, has considered the same that if in such a gathering that too in the Court proceeding, the father has behaved like this with his daughter then what to say regarding his harsh and cruel behavior towards his daughter in his house. 
21. The girl/wife has expressed her wish to go along with her husband upon the queries of her father where she wants to go. She has stated twice that she will go along with her husband to his native place at Ichagarh, Hazaribagh. 
22. After all, the girl is major and she has shown, without any compulsion, in course of interaction with the Court, her willingness to live with her husband in presence of her parents and as such, in view of the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Shafin Jahan v. Asokan K.M.,
(2018) 16 SCC 368 where the wish of the girl is to be taken care of, if the girl is major and the marriage has been solemnized. In the aforesaid Judgment the Hon'ble Apex Court while referring the ratio of Gian Devi v. Nari Niketan , (1976) 3 SCC 234 has observed that where an individual is over eighteen years of age, no fetters could be placed on her choice on where to reside or about the person with whom she could stay. For ready reference the relevant paragraph of the aforesaid judgment is being quoted as under:
74. The principles which underlie the exercise of the jurisdiction of a court in a habeas corpus petition have been reiterated in several decisions of the Court. 
In Gian Devi v. Nari Niketan [Gian Devi v. Nari Niketan, (1976) 3 SCC 234 : 1976 SCC (Cri) 387] , a three-Judge Bench observed that where an individual is over eighteen years of age, no fetters could be placed on her choice on where to reside or about the person with whom she could stay : (SCC p.
235, para 7) "7. ... Whatever may be the date of birth of the petitioner, the fact remains that she is at present more than 18 years of age. As the petitioner is sui juris no fetters can be placed upon her choice of the person with whom she is to stay, nor can any restriction be imposed regarding the place where she should stay. The court or the relatives of the petitioner can also not substitute their opinion or preference for that of the petitioner in such a matter." 
23. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mohd. Ikram Hussain v. State of U.P., 1963 SCC OnLine SC 17 has observed that the writ of habeas corpus issues not only for release from detention by the State but also for release from private detention and a remedy of writ of habeas corpus is available to the husband for regaining the custody of his wife if she is wrongfully detained by anyone from him without her consent, for ready reference the relevant paragraph is being quoted as under:
12. ---- The writ of habeas corpus issues not only for release from detention by the State but also for release from private detention. At Common Law a writ of habeas corpus was available to the husband for regaining the custody of his wife if she was wrongfully detained by anyone from him without her consent. 
Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105646308/
7 What amounts to wrongful detention of the wife is, of course, a question for the Court to decide in each case and different circumstances may exist either entitling or disentitling a husband to this remedy. ---
24. At this juncture, in the background of the aforesaid fact this Court would like to refer the guidelines to entertain the writ of Habeas Corpus for police protection which has been rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Devu G Nair V. The State of Kerala & Others (2024) Live Law (SC) 249. For ready reference, relevant paragraph16 is being reproduced as under:
"16. Guidelines for the courts in dealing with habeas corpus petitions or petitions for police protection are formulated below:
a. Habeas corpus petitions and petitions for protection filed by a partner, friend or a natal family member must be given a priority in listing and hearing before the court. 
A court must avoid adjourning the matter, or delays in the disposal of the case;
b. In evaluating the locus standi of a partner or friend, the court must not make a roving enquiry into the precise nature of the relationship between the appellant and the person;
c. The effort must be to create an environment conducive for a free and uncoerced dialogue to ascertain the wishes of the corpus;
d. The court must ensure that the corpus is produced before the court and given the opportunity to interact with the judges in-person in chambers to ensure the privacy and safety of the detained or missing person. The court must conduct in-camera proceedings. The recording of the statement must be transcribed and the recording must be secured to ensure that it is not accessible to any other party;
e. The court must ensure that the wishes of the detained person is not unduly influenced by the Court, or the police, or the natal family during the course of the proceedings. In particular, the court must ensure that the individuals(s) alleged to be detaining the individual against their volition are not present in the same environment as the detained or missing person. Similarly, in petitions seeking police protection from the natal family of the parties, the family must not be placed in the same environment as the petitioners; f. Upon securing the environment and inviting the detained or missing person in chambers, the court must make active efforts to put the detained or missing person at ease. The preferred name and pronouns of the detained or missing person may be asked. The person must be given a comfortable seating, access to drinking water and washroom. They must be allowed to take periodic breaks to collect themselves. The judge must adopt a friendly and compassionate demeanor and make all efforts to defuse any tension or discomfort. 
Courts must ensure that the detained or missing person faces no obstacles in being able to express their wishes to the court;
Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105646308/
8 g. A court while dealing with the detained or missing person may ascertain the age of the detained or missing person. However, the minority of the detained or missing person must not be used, at the threshold, to dismiss a habeas corpus petition against illegal detention by a natal family;
h. The judges must showcase sincere empathy and compassion for the case of the detained or missing person. Social morality laden with homophobic or transphobic views or any personal predilection of the judge or sympathy for the natal family must be eschewed. The court must ensure that the law is followed in ascertaining the free will of the detained or missing person;
i. If a detained or missing person expresses their wish to not go back to the alleged detainer or the natal family, then the person must be released immediately without any further delay;
j. -------
k. -----"
25. Herein it has been admitted by the parents of the girl and the learned counsel appearing for the Respondent No.6 (father of the girl) about the marriage of petitioner with the girl (daughter of Respondent No.6) reason being that the petition has been filed in the concerned court under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act for declaring the said marriage as nullity, the moment such petition has been filed, it means that the issue of marriage has been admitted. 
26. Both the petitioner and the girl are major and have solemnized marriage on their own wish and not only that in course of interaction it has come from the mouth of the girl that she has also spent a whole night with the petitioner/the husband. 
27. This Court, considering all these things and taking into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, is of the view that when the marriage has been admitted, no one can come in the way of husband and wife by way a preventive measure or any prohibition in leading the life as husband and wife unlawfully and forcefully. 
28. The petitioner, in course of interaction, has stated that he has solemnized marriage with the girl and he will take all care being the husband so that the girl, who happens to be the wife of the petitioner, may lead her life with full dignity in her in-laws house. But, he has expressed the fear of untoward happening since threatening has been given by the father and family members to the family members of the petitioner. The same thing has also been stated by the girl, the wife of the petitioner. 
29. It further appears from the order dated 01.08.2024 passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court wherein the father of the girl has admitted that it is the question of their honour as they belong from a different caste than that of the boy.
Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105646308/
9 30. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the Respondent No.6 that a petition under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act has been filed before the concerned court. 
31. This Court has posed a pinpointed query that when the marriage has been solemnized in the month of April, 2024 then why immediately thereafter no application was filed and why it has been filed once the father has admitted, as has been taken note in the order dated 01.08.2024 wherein the father himself has admitted regarding the question of honour as they belong from a different caste than that of the boy. 
32. The question is that if the girl is major and willing to live with the husband who is also major then where is the question of honour of the family. 
33. The Coordinate Bench has shown the concern as has been taken note in the order dated 01.08.2024 as under paragraphs 6 and 7 wherein the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad has been directed to look into the issue of security of the girl and the family members of the petitioner,
for ready reference paragraphs 6 and 7 of order dated 01.08.2024 are being referred hereunder as :-
"6. We direct the Senior Superintendent of Police Dhanbad, to initiate an enquiry and submit a report to this Court in a sealed cover about the allegation of torture, threat and threat perception upon the petitioner and his parents or other family members from the side of family members of the corpus. 
7. It is made clear that the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad, will make the parents of the girl understand that if any untowards incident happens to the girl or any of the family members of the petitioner, they will be primarily held responsible. 
The Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad, will ensure safety of the corpus/girl and the petitioner/boy and will take appropriate measures as per the situation."
34. A report has been submitted by the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad in pursuance to the order dated 01.08.2024.
35. We have perused the said report and found therefrom that the element of threatening is there having been given by the father and the family members of the girl to the petitioner and his family members. 
36. In the report submitted by the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad, it has been stated that the marriage said to be solemnized with the present petitioner is on misconception and by duping the girl on the promise to provide job. 
37. It appears from the said report that the enquiry which has been conducted by the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad, the statement has not been recorded in conducive and congenial atmosphere and in isolation, rather, it appears that such statement has been taken in presence of the family members because when we interacted with the girl, the statement given by her to the police has been reversed and she had negated her entire versions recorded by police. 
Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105646308/
10 38. The petition which has been filed under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act also narrates the same thing which has been taken note in the report by the Senior Superintendent of Police,
Dhanbad. But, when we have interacted with the girl, she clarified all the position which has been taken note by this Court hereinabove. 
39. This Court, therefore, considering the version of the girl who has expressed to live along with his husband, hereby directs the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad to look into the issue of threatening and security of the family members of the present petitioner by taking personal care so that no mis-happening or untoward incident occur to the family members of the petitioner. 
40. The petitioner has submitted that although he lives in Dhanbad for earning his livelihood but if his wife will accompany him, he will go to his native place which is situated within the jurisdiction of Ichak Police Station in the district of Hazaribagh.
41. Considering the fact in entirety and taking into consideration the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court as discussed and referred hereinabove, since, the girl has expressed her wish to live with her husband on the basis of the marriage solemnized and the marriage is admitted one, this Court is of the view the girl is major and want to lead her life according to her own free will and in that view of the matter, if she wants to live with her husband no one can put restriction upon the same.
42. Accordingly and as per the wish, the girl since has shown her willingness to live with her husband and the petitioner is ready to live along with his wife, hence no direction needs to be passed in this regard. 
43. Let them go jointly from here.
44. The Superintendent of Police, Hazaribagh is directed to look into the issue of security where the petitioner along with his wife are to live, i.e., within the jurisdiction of Ichak Police Station in the district of Hazaribagh so that no untoward incident takes place. 
45. It is made clear that if any untoward event will be there, the Superintendent of Police,
Hazaribagh will be personally accountable for the same. 
46. The Superintendent of Police, Hazaribagh is further directed to communicate this order to the Officer-in-Charge of the Ichak Police Station to take care of the security issue. 
47. Mr. Anand Kumar Sinha, learned counsel appearing for the Respondent No.6, the father of the girl, has finally submitted that he also wants that the girl, who is the wife of the present petitioner,
should lead happy married life. 
48. The said submission has been appreciated by this Court. 
49. Mr. Mr. Deepankar Roy, learned AC to G.A.-III appearing for the State, has undertaken to communicate this order to the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad and Superintendent of Dhananjay Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand & Others on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105646308/
11 Police, Hazaribagh forthwith. 
50. The Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad has stated that one Inspector will accompany the petitioner and his wife so that they safely reach to their native place, i.e., Ichak, Hazaribagh. 
51. At this juncture, the girl has disclosed that her mobile phone, study materials etc. are lying in Dhanbad. Upon this, the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad has undertaken to send all belongings of the girl including the mobile phone and study material to the house of her in- laws in Ichak, Hazaribagh. 
52. When this Court has passed the order then the girl, the wife of the present petitioner, has requested the Court that she wants to convey something to the Court. 
53. The Court asked to the girl as to whether she is willing to allow the petitioner-her husband to remain here, she has stated that he may be allowed to be there but all the counsel including the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad has been requested to remain absent.
54. The girl/wife has stated showing the anxiety that what will happen to the petition which has been filed in the concerned court under Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act which according to her, has been filed on coercion forcefully. 
55. She has stated that she is going to live with her husband, hence such petition is meaningless and as such, she does not want to press the same. 
56. This Court, after having considered the same, is of the view that let this order be placed before the court concerned through a legal aid counsel to do the needful. 
57. Let this order be communicated to the Secretary, DLSA, Dhanbad, Secretary, DLSA, Hazaribagh and the Member Secretary, JHALSA with a direction to extend all kinds of legal aid to the girl as and when required. 
58. The purpose of this Habeas Corpus has been fulfilled but on the issue of security of the petitioner and his family members as well as the girl, the matter is being posted on 16.12.2024 at 10:30 AM in Chamber for further update both from the Senior Superintendent of Police, Dhanbad as well as Superintendent of Police, Hazaribagh. 
(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Navneet Kumar, J.) Birendra/ A.F.R.
